newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 96 consumer imports down, capital goods up.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 96 consumer imports down, capital goods up.

text.p: Brazilian imports of consumer goods slumped 11.0 percent in 1996 over 1995 while imports of capital goods and fuels and lubricants surged, the Finance Ministry said in a statement.

The ministry said consumer goods purchases totalled $9.719 billion last year compared to $10.917 billion in 1995. The main contributor to the drop were car imports, which at $1.562 billion were 48.6 percent lower than the year before.
Fuels and lubricants imports were up 19.4 percent at $6.227 billion in 1996 while capital goods purchases rose 12.1 percent to $12.704 billion.
Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, economic policy secretary at the Finance Ministry, told reporters the capital goods imports were positive and boded well for future exports.
He said fuel imports were probably due to higher consumer demand in the second half of 1996.

Mauricio Cortes, secretary of foreign trade at the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, pointed out the economy expanded 6.52 percent in third quarter 1996, admittedly against a very low comparative 1995 base but nevertheless the highest quarterly growth rate recorded since 1980.
The main component of Brazil's 1996 imports were raw materials and semimanufactured products, which at $24.636 billion accounted for 46.2 percent of total imports of $53.286 billion.
In 1995, $22.393 billion in imported raw materials and semimanufactured products made up 44.9 percent of total imports of $49.858 billion, the statement said.
